public_rationale: OpenAI's January 18, 2026 disclosure describes consumer subscriptions, workplace subscriptions, and API services [e1]. It does not provide a comparable large-business revenue series through 2030 or the realized annual revenue outcome for 2030 [e1]. These revenue channels alone establish neither an absence of sustained large-business growth nor achievement of the target without that growth [e1]. The evidence therefore leaves the conditional forecast unresolved [e1].
limitations: The contract's December 31, 2030 deadline is after the October 28, 2026 evaluation date.
The absence of sustained large-business revenue growth has not been established. No qualifying early-resolution event is documented.
The contract uses approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue for calendar 2030. The source leaves the precise threshold and large-business customer definition ambiguous.
A revenue target miss alone would not support the forecast. The absence of sustained large-business revenue growth must also be established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI cannot reach its ambitious revenue numbers (13x-ing current revenue in five years) unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up.
conditions: unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up

statement.excerpt: Needless to say, OpenAI can’t make its ambitious revenue numbers — 13x-ing current revenue in five years — unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up and up and up and up and up.

from_speaker: can’t make its ambitious revenue numbers
unless revenue from paying big business customers keeps going up
our_interpretation: Read the statement as a necessary-condition forecast: if large-business revenue does not keep growing, OpenAI will not reach the stated total-revenue target.
The conditional antecedent is failure of sustained large-business revenue growth, not the occurrence of growth.
Use approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue during calendar 2030 as the target supplied by the surrounding passage.
Use December 31, 2030 as the latest deadline permitted by the named year.
Interpret repeated 'going up' as sustained growth across the forecast period, rather than growth every day or month.
The financial target is a press-reported estimate, not a specified GAAP measure.
criteria.support_condition: If the absence of sustained large-business revenue growth is established, OpenAI falls short of approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue in 2030.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI achieves approximately $200 billion in realized annual revenue by the deadline despite an established absence of sustained large-business revenue growth.

evidence.locator: Paragraph describing the evolution of OpenAI's business model
evidence.explanation: The CFO describes consumer subscriptions alongside workplace subscriptions, APIs, and commerce. Multiple revenue channels make segment evidence necessary; their existence does not show that the target can be reached without large-business growth.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable total and large-business revenue records through 2030 would establish whether the condition occurred. If sustained large-business growth is absent, realized annual revenue below approximately $200 billion in 2030 would support the forecast; achieving the target would contradict it. Early contradiction requires documented achievement of the annual revenue target without sustained large-business growth. Early support requires irreversible cessation of OpenAI's revenue-generating business, with the absence of sustained large-business growth independently established.
